overview:
Mississippi's 3rd District is a strongly Republican seat, and Michael Guest is seeking another term as its incumbent. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, roughly $1 million on hand, while Democrat Michael Chiaradio has raised about $208,000 and has limited cash remaining. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so expectations rest on the district's partisan lean and the candidates' resources. Prediction markets give Guest roughly a 98 percent chance of winning. The forecast expects Guest to prevail by a comfortable double-digit margin, consistent with how the district has voted in recent cycles, though uncertainty is wider than usual because of the absence of polling.
